lessons.title: At the airport

words.meaning: The document that lets you board.
words.example: Have your boarding pass ready.
Our flight is delayed by an hour.

words.meaning: The second flight of a journey.
words.example: I have a connecting flight in Doha.

words.meaning: Officials who check what you bring in.
words.example: We were held at customs.
I prefer an aisle seat.

listen: Attention passengers: flight BA204 to London is delayed by forty minutes.
Please have your passport and boarding pass ready at the gate.
speak: I have a connecting flight, so I need to hurry.
Could I have an aisle seat, please?

grammar.title: Present continuous for arrangements
grammar.rule: Use am, is or are plus -ing for fixed future arrangements.
examples: I am flying to Rome on Tuesday.
We are meeting the client at nine.
She is not coming this week.

quiz.prompt: Choose the arrangement.
options: I fly to Rome on Tuesday.
I am flying to Rome on Tuesday.
quiz.explanation: A fixed plan uses the present continuous.

quiz.prompt: Complete: The flight ___ delayed by an hour.
quiz.explanation: Delayed is an adjective here.

quiz.prompt: Which word means the second flight of a journey?

lessons.title: Hotel problems

words.meaning: To say you are not satisfied.
words.example: I had to complain about the noise.
They offered a partial refund.
The air conditioning is faulty.
They gave us a free upgrade.
The manager apologised.

listen: I am sorry about the noise. I can move you to a quieter room on the fifth floor.
The heating in room 212 is faulty and nobody has come to fix it.
speak: I would like to complain about the noise.
Could you move me to another room, please?

grammar.title: Polite requests and complaints
grammar.rule: Could, would and I am afraid make a complaint firm but polite.
examples: Could you send someone up?
I am afraid there is a problem.
Would it be possible to change rooms?

quiz.prompt: Which is the most polite?
quiz.explanation: Could plus please is the polite form.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I am ___ there has been a mistake.
quiz.explanation: I am afraid softens bad news.

quiz.prompt: Which word means not working properly?

lessons.title: Telling a story

words.example: Suddenly the lights went out.

words.meaning: In the end, after a long time.
words.example: Eventually the taxi arrived.

words.meaning: To understand something for the first time.
words.example: I realised I had left my bag.
Meanwhile, my friend was waiting outside.

words.meaning: To end in a certain way.
words.example: It turned out fine.

listen: I was waiting at the bus stop when it suddenly started to rain.
While I was looking for my keys, my phone was ringing in my pocket.
speak: I was walking home when I met an old friend.
Eventually we found the right street.

grammar.title: Past continuous with past simple
grammar.rule: The long action uses was or were plus -ing, the short interrupting one uses past simple.
examples: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were sleeping when we arrived.
While she was driving, it started to snow.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ dinner when he called.
quiz.explanation: The long action takes the past continuous.

quiz.prompt: Complete: While we were walking, it ___ to rain.
quiz.explanation: The short action takes the past simple.

quiz.prompt: Which word means at the same time?

lessons.title: In a meeting

words.meaning: The list of things to discuss.
words.example: The agenda has four items.
We moved the deadline to Friday.
I will follow up by email.
Security is our priority.
Let me clarify that point.

listen: Quick update: the client moved the deadline, so testing starts on Monday.
Before we finish, can someone follow up with the design team?
speak: Could you clarify that point, please?
I think our priority should be the deadline.

grammar.title: Giving opinions
grammar.rule: Soften an opinion with I think, in my view, or it seems to me.
examples: I think we should wait.
In my view the deadline is too tight.
It seems to me that we need more data.

quiz.prompt: Which sounds most professional?
options: I see it a little differently.
quiz.explanation: Softening keeps the discussion open.

quiz.prompt: Complete: Let me ___ that point.
quiz.explanation: Clarify is the verb.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ we should wait for the data.
quiz.explanation: Opinions use present simple.

lessons.title: Writing an email

words.example: I am writing regarding your invoice.

words.meaning: To send a file with a message.
words.example: I have attached the report.
Please confirm the time.
I would like to request two days off.

words.meaning: A formal way to end a letter.
words.example: Yours sincerely, Ana.

listen: Dear Mr Shah, I am writing regarding the invoice sent last week.
Please confirm whether Thursday at ten works for you.
speak: I am writing to request one day off.
Please find the report attached.

grammar.title: Formal and informal register
grammar.rule: Formal writing avoids contractions and uses fuller phrases.
examples: Informal: Can you send it? Formal: Could you please send it?
Informal: Thanks! Formal: Thank you for your time.
Informal: I'm sorry. Formal: I apologise for the delay.

quiz.prompt: Which opening is formal?
quiz.explanation: Dear plus surname is standard formal.

quiz.prompt: Choose the formal version.
quiz.explanation: Could you please is the polite formal request.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I have ___ the document.
quiz.explanation: Have plus past participle.

lessons.title: Job interview

words.example: My main strength is planning.
My biggest achievement was the launch.
I was responsible for the budget.
The biggest challenge was the timeline.
I am motivated by solving problems.

listen: Tell me about a time when a project did not go to plan.
I was responsible for a team of four and we delivered two weeks early.
speak: My biggest strength is that I stay calm under pressure.
I was responsible for the whole reporting process.

grammar.title: Present perfect for experience
grammar.rule: Use have or has plus the past participle when the time is not stated.
examples: I have managed a team of five.
She has worked in three countries.
Have you ever led a project?

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: A stated past time takes the past simple.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ managed a team before.
quiz.explanation: I takes have.

quiz.prompt: Which word means something difficult that tests you?

lessons.title: Agreeing and disagreeing

words.example: That is a fair point.
However, the cost is high.
Exactly, that is what I meant.
I partly agree with you.
You have convinced me.

listen: I take your point, however I am not sure the numbers support it.
That is exactly what I was going to say.
speak: I partly agree, but I would add one thing.
That is a fair point, however I see it differently.

grammar.title: Linking words
grammar.rule: However, although and despite join contrasting ideas in different ways.
examples: It was expensive. However, it was worth it.
Although it was expensive, it was worth it.
Despite the price, it was worth it.

quiz.prompt: Complete: ___ it rained, we enjoyed the day.
quiz.explanation: Although starts a clause with a subject and verb.

quiz.prompt: Complete: ___ the rain, we enjoyed the day.
quiz.explanation: Despite is followed by a noun.

quiz.prompt: Which word shows partial agreement?

lessons.title: If this, then that

words.example: We will go unless it rains.

words.meaning: To be decided by something else.
words.example: It depends on the price.
The consequence was a delay.

words.meaning: To think something is true without proof.
words.example: Do not assume they know.

words.meaning: Good enough for the cost or effort.
words.example: The extra hour was worth it.

listen: If the client approves today, we can start on Monday.
If I had more time, I would rewrite the whole section.
speak: If I have time tomorrow, I will call you.
If I were you, I would take the job.

grammar.title: First and second conditional
grammar.rule: Real future: if plus present, will plus base. Imagined: if plus past, would plus base.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
If I had more money, I would travel.
If I were you, I would apply.

quiz.prompt: Complete: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel.
quiz.explanation: After if use the present, not will.

quiz.prompt: Complete: If I ___ rich, I would buy a house.
quiz.explanation: Were is standard in the second conditional.

quiz.prompt: Complete: We will go ___ it rains.
quiz.explanation: Unless means if not.

lessons.title: Describing change

words.example: Prices rose gradually.
There was a significant drop.
The trend is clear.
Traffic doubled in two years.
Sales declined last quarter.

listen: Between 2019 and 2023 the number of remote workers more than doubled.
After the change, complaints declined significantly.
speak: The number of users increased gradually last year.
There was a significant decline in the second half.

grammar.title: The passive voice
grammar.rule: Be plus past participle, used when the action matters more than who did it.
examples: The report was sent yesterday.
English is spoken in many countries.
The rule has been changed.

quiz.prompt: Make it passive: Someone changed the rule.
quiz.explanation: Was plus changed.

quiz.prompt: Complete: The email ___ this morning.
quiz.explanation: The email did not send itself.

quiz.prompt: Which word means to become twice as much?

lessons.title: At the bank

words.meaning: An arrangement to keep money at a bank.
words.example: I opened an account last week.

words.meaning: To move money from one account to another.
words.example: The transfer takes two days.
I withdrew cash at the airport.

words.meaning: A list of what went in and out of an account.
words.example: Check last month's statement.

words.meaning: Permission to spend more than you have.
words.example: The overdraft has a high fee.

listen: The transfer went out on Monday, but it will not show on their statement until Wednesday.
There is no fee to withdraw at our machines, but other banks may charge you.
speak: I would like to open an account.
Could you check my last statement, please?

grammar.title: Present perfect with already, yet and just
grammar.rule: Already goes before the participle, yet at the end of questions and negatives.
examples: I have already paid.
Have you paid yet?
It has just arrived.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I have ___ transferred the money.
quiz.explanation: Already goes before the participle.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Yet goes at the end of a question.

quiz.prompt: Which word means to take money out?

lessons.title: Bills and contracts

words.meaning: An amount you are asked to pay.
words.example: There is a charge for late payment.

words.meaning: Expected or required by a certain time.
words.example: The payment is due on the fifth.

words.meaning: To extend something for another period.
words.example: The contract renews automatically.
Read the terms before you sign.
They sent an estimate, not a final bill.

listen: Your contract renews on the first of next month unless you cancel before then.
That charge looks wrong to me. The estimate we agreed was forty pounds lower.
speak: I think this charge is a mistake.
When exactly is the payment due?

grammar.title: Modals of obligation: must, have to, should
grammar.rule: Must and have to mean it is required. Should means it is advisable, not compulsory.
examples: You must sign here.
I have to renew it in May.
You should read the terms.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence is advice, not a rule?
quiz.explanation: Should gives advice.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ renew the contract before Friday.
quiz.explanation: Have to expresses obligation.

quiz.prompt: Which word means an approximate cost?

lessons.title: Disputing a charge

words.example: I want to dispute this charge.

words.meaning: Something that shows a claim is true.
words.example: I have proof that I cancelled.

words.meaning: To push for an answer that has not come.
words.example: I had to chase it up twice.

words.meaning: A number used to find a record.
words.example: Quote the reference in your email.
They resolved it within a day.

listen: I understand you are frustrated. Give me the reference number and I will look at it now.
If we cannot resolve it today, I will pass it to the complaints team for you.
speak: I would like to dispute a charge on my account.
I have already chased this up twice.

grammar.title: Complaining politely with softeners
grammar.rule: I am afraid, there seems to be and I think there may be turn an accusation into a report.
examples: I am afraid there is a problem.
There seems to be an error.
I think there may be a mistake.

quiz.prompt: Which complaint is the most polite?
options: There seems to be an error on my bill.
quiz.explanation: Seems to be softens the claim.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I am ___ there has been a mistake.
quiz.explanation: I am afraid is a fixed polite phrase.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase means to push for an answer that has not come?

lessons.title: Describing symptoms

words.example: I have had a dull ache all week.
My throat has been sore since Monday.
I felt dizzy when I stood up.

words.meaning: Larger than normal because of injury.
words.example: My ankle is swollen.
It got worse steadily over the week.

listen: It started about four days ago as a sore throat, and gradually became a cough.
Any dizziness? Only when I stand up quickly, not otherwise.
speak: I have had a sore throat for four days.
It gets worse in the evening.

grammar.title: For and since with the present perfect
grammar.rule: For marks a length of time. Since marks the point it started.
examples: I have had it for three days.
I have had it since Monday.
She has been ill since the weekend.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I have had this cough ___ two weeks.
quiz.explanation: Two weeks is a length of time.

quiz.prompt: Complete: She has felt unwell ___ Tuesday.
quiz.explanation: Tuesday is a starting point.

quiz.prompt: Which word means slowly over time?

lessons.title: Giving and taking advice

words.meaning: To stop activity so your body recovers.
words.example: You should rest for a day or two.
Avoid heavy lifting this week.

words.meaning: To reduce the amount of something.
words.example: I am trying to cut down on sugar.

words.meaning: Good enough to justify the effort.
words.example: It is worth seeing a doctor.

words.meaning: If not, or in other respects.
words.example: Rest now, otherwise it will drag on.

listen: If I were you, I would cut down on coffee for a week and see whether it helps.
It is probably nothing, but it is worth getting it checked.
speak: If I were you, I would rest.
It is worth seeing someone about it.

grammar.title: Second conditional for advice
grammar.rule: If I were you, I would is the standard way to advise without ordering.
examples: If I were you, I would wait.
If I had that pain, I would call someone.
If it were mine, I would replace it.

quiz.prompt: Complete: If I ___ you, I would rest.
quiz.explanation: The fixed phrase uses were.

quiz.prompt: Complete: It is worth ___ a doctor.
quiz.explanation: Worth takes -ing.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase means to reduce something?

lessons.title: Saying no politely

words.example: I had to bow out of the project.

words.meaning: Something you have promised to do.
words.example: I have a commitment that evening.

words.meaning: The amount you are able to take on.
words.example: I do not have capacity this month.

words.meaning: To move something to a different time.
words.example: Could we reschedule for next week?
I appreciate you asking me.

listen: I really appreciate the offer, but I do not have capacity before the end of the month.
I cannot make Thursday. Could we reschedule to the following week instead?
speak: I appreciate the offer, but I cannot this month.
Could we reschedule for next week?

grammar.title: Softening a refusal
grammar.rule: Thank first, refuse second, offer an alternative third. The order does most of the work.
examples: Thanks for thinking of me, but I cannot this time.
I would love to, but I am not free until June.
I cannot do Thursday - would Monday work?

quiz.prompt: Which refusal is the most professional?
options: Thanks for asking, but I do not have capacity this month.
quiz.explanation: Thank, refuse, explain.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ the offer, but I have to decline.
quiz.explanation: Appreciate means to be grateful for.

quiz.prompt: Which word means to move something to another time?

lessons.title: When technology fails

words.example: The app crashes when I open photos.

words.meaning: To stop responding while still on.
words.example: The screen froze for a minute.

words.meaning: To turn something off and on again.
words.example: Restarting fixed it.

words.meaning: The options that control how something works.
words.example: Check your notification settings.

words.meaning: Able to work with something else.
words.example: The cable is not compatible.

listen: It freezes for about ten seconds and then crashes completely. Restarting helps for an hour.
That model is not compatible with the newer charger, which is probably your problem.
speak: The app crashes when I open it.
I restarted it, but the problem came back.

grammar.title: Describing repeated problems with present simple and continuous
grammar.rule: Present simple for what always happens, continuous for a temporary phase.
examples: It crashes every time.
It keeps freezing this week.
It is doing it again.

quiz.prompt: Which describes something that always happens?
options: It crashes every time I open it.
quiz.explanation: Present simple describes a general truth.

quiz.prompt: Complete: It ___ freezing since the update.
quiz.explanation: Keeps plus -ing describes a repeated problem.

quiz.prompt: Which word means able to work with something else?

lessons.title: Talking about the news

words.example: Apparently the road will close in May.

words.meaning: To say something is true without proving it.
words.example: The report claims the figure is higher.

words.meaning: A source of information you can trust.
words.example: Is that a reliable source?

words.meaning: To make something sound bigger than it is.
words.example: The headline exaggerates the risk.
They updated the story an hour later.

listen: Apparently they have updated the story twice, and the original claim is not in it any more.
I would not repeat that until we see it from a reliable source.
speak: Apparently the decision has been delayed.
I am not sure that is a reliable source.

grammar.title: Reporting what you are not sure about
grammar.rule: Apparently, reportedly and it is said that mark information you have not verified.
examples: Apparently they cancelled it.
It is said to be the largest.
Reportedly, nobody was hurt.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence shows the speaker is not certain?
quiz.explanation: Apparently marks second-hand information.

quiz.prompt: Complete: The article ___ that prices will fall.
quiz.explanation: The article is it, so the verb takes -s.

quiz.prompt: Which word means to make something sound bigger than it is?

lessons.title: Explaining something technical

words.meaning: Used to introduce a simple summary.
words.example: Basically, it stores your files remotely.

words.meaning: Used to say something a second, simpler way.
words.example: In other words, it is a backup.
For instance, photos and documents.
It takes roughly ten minutes.
The setup is straightforward.

listen: Basically it keeps a copy elsewhere. In other words, if this laptop dies, nothing is lost.
It takes roughly ten minutes, and the setup itself is straightforward.
speak: Basically, it keeps a copy of everything.
For instance, your photos and documents.

grammar.title: Sequencing and clarifying an explanation
grammar.rule: First, then and finally order the steps. In other words and for instance make them land.
examples: First you install it.
Then it runs in the background.
Finally, you can restore anything.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase introduces an example?
quiz.explanation: For instance introduces an example.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase restates something more simply?
quiz.explanation: In other words restates.

quiz.prompt: Which word means easy to understand?
